question.text: Govind, a resident non-senior citizen, has a total income of Rs.4,80,000 under the old tax regime for FY 2024-25. His tax computed on total income is Rs.11,500. What is his tax liability after applying Section 87A rebate?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the old regime, Section 87A allows a rebate to a resident individual whose total income does not exceed Rs.5,00,000, equal to the lower of the actual tax payable and Rs.12,500. Govind is a resident individual with total income of Rs.4,80,000 (below the Rs.5,00,000 threshold) and tax of Rs.11,500. Applying the lower-of test, the rebate is min(Rs.11,500, Rs.12,500) = Rs.11,500, which wipes out the tax. Net liability = Rs.0. The Trap: Option B wrongly denies the rebate. Option C makes an arithmetic error. Option D treats Rs.12,500 as a fixed rebate amount rather than a cap; the rebate is limited to the actual tax payable and cannot exceed it. Note: Section 87A under the old regime requires resident status and total income up to Rs.5,00,000. The rebate is the lower of actual tax and Rs.12,500.
